goal: Evaluate passage-first, self-contained PDF anthologies with source-provenance, verified in-text editorial highlights, and genuine sermon-communication analysis

cases.prompt: Run Passage Prep for Matthew 5:4 using John Piper and David Platt on my pastor list. Make a Google Doc for iPad reading, without writing my sermon.
cases.expected: Two-part reader including lawfully reproduced historical sources plus verified sermons; Piper 1986 direct passage; Platt 2024 clearly only recaps verse 4
assertions: Two main parts in commentary-then-sermon order
Commentary highlights occur in verified original wording and are legally reusable
Piper 1986 identified as Matthew 5:3–4 sermon and its student/crutch illustration accurately classified
Platt The Good Life Redefined is labeled Matthew 5:7–12 sermon with brief 5:4 recap, not direct 5:4 sermon
Full sermon flow tied to transcript sections, including placement/function of actual illustrations
No final AI sermon manuscript or imposed preaching points

cases.prompt: Passage Prep John 11:17–44 for pastoral sermon prep; preserve actual commentary text and show the flow in trusted sermons.
cases.expected: Grief sensitive, source grounded reader; no claim that specific bereavements are punishments for sin
assertions: John 11 interpreted in narrative context and linked to Jesus' tears
Commentary viewpoints kept attributable with legal excerpts
Only genuine John 11 messages get full sermon maps
No conflation of grief with personal culpability
Reader has annotation space and sources linked

cases.prompt: Passage Prep 1 Samuel 18:1–16. Keep narrative sequence clear, do not preach it for me.
cases.expected: Narrative-aware commentary and source-verified sermon maps; show honest gaps
assertions: Part 1 preserves sequential narrative movements and distinguishes author interpretation
No story illustration made up to fill sermon-flow gaps
Adjacent Jonathan/David sermon correctly labeled SURROUNDING if not exact
Modern copyrighted commentary not pasted in full
No generated sermon outline presented as the user's final outline

cases.prompt: Passage Prep on 3 John 1:13–15. Search the two approved pastors, John Piper and David Platt, only.
cases.expected: Accurate scarcity reporting; no false direct-text sermons
assertions: Only Piper and Platt searched as approved roster
No unrelated topical sermons claimed to be exact passage exposition
Unavailable sermon coverage reported honestly
Part 1 prioritizes relevant reliable commentary, even if few sources
Clear original manuscript vs metadata-only distinction

cases.prompt: Passage Prep for Romans 8:18–30. I supplied a modern copyrighted Logos commentary excerpt; integrate it into my personal reader and find Piper/Platt sermons.
cases.expected: Respect license restrictions while offering useful user-readable source pointers and reader notes
assertions: Modern commentary permissions assessed rather than presumed
Any copyrighted verbatim external quotations are short and attributed
User-supplied material treated as personal-study content, not published to a public repo
Source notes explain exactly what is accessible
Sermon illustrations cite original manuscripts and are classified

cases.prompt: Passage Prep for Luke 15:11–32, just the commentary reading section. No sermon research this time.
cases.expected: User's explicit one-part override takes precedence
assertions: Only Part 1 generated, without redundant sermon-section filler
Commentary texts in own words only if legally permissible
Highlights sparse and anchored
No assistant-proposed sermon or interpretation
Reader usable to annotate

cases.prompt: Write a polished 30-minute sermon manuscript on Matthew 5:4 using my outline.
cases.expected: Passage Prep does not override an explicitly requested sermon-writing workflow
assertions: No unsolicited two-part reading packet
Does not misrepresent a commissioned sermon as sourced commentary
Does not activate the source-collection skill in place of a sermon-writing request
Does not present invented quotations from named pastors

cases.prompt: Run Passage Prep on Psalm 23 using Josh Howerton, John Piper and Timothy Keller. Do not waste resources deriving video timestamps.
cases.expected: Lakepointe direct-site search, honest differences in manuscript accessibility; no fabricated video-only structure
assertions: Checks lakepointe.church/messages first for Josh Howerton rather than sweeping generic web
Confirms the speaker is Josh Howerton, not a different Lakepointe team member
If no real transcript or inspected media, does not fabricate full movements or an illustration
No unverified minute/second timestamp or constructed deep link
Keller is searched at gospelinlife.com/sermons; recording-only availability is identified

cases.prompt: Run Passage Prep for Acts 2:1–13 with Philip Anthony Mitchell, Jim Cymbala, Derwin Gray and Francis Chan. Use only solid source evidence; timestamps optional.
cases.expected: Routes to 2819 official media, Brooklyn Tabernacle media, Transformation Church sermon outlines and Crazy Love; honors video-only limitations
assertions: Visits direct archives named for all four speakers before any broad discovery
Distinguishes official published outlines from full transcripts and third-party transcription
Marks any unsupported sermon-map stage or personal anecdote as unavailable
Does not misattribute guest speakers to user-selected pastors
Omission of unverified timestamps is treated as correct behavior

cases.prompt: Find Commentary Reading Room sources for Matthew 6:9–13 from Andrew Murray, Matthew Henry, Thomas Watson and Robert Murray M’Cheyne; exact source words where lawful.
cases.expected: Finds relevant verified public-domain material without disguising theme-only devotional text as verse-by-verse commentary
assertions: Andrew Murray passages are confirmed in an actual book rather than made up
Matthew Henry is routed to CCEL full commentary first
M’Cheyne is identified as Robert Murray M’Cheyne, not a modern missionary named McKinney
Specific historic editions/copyright status are identified before reproducing long text
Part 1 allows user annotation and visible attribution

cases.prompt: Run Passage Prep for Matthew 5:4 with John Stott and Tim Keller. Include verified timestamps only if already available, and use my Logos only if accessible.
cases.expected: Text scarcity acknowledged, licensed Logos transcripts not assumed accessible, timestamps not fabricated
assertions: John Stott official sermons are searched via johnstott.org
Logos Sermon Archive is described as licensed with transcripts, not free public-domain
Gospel in Life uses official Scripture filtering
Timestamps included only when independently verified in exact recording
Reader can still be completed with links when full transcripts are inaccessible

cases.prompt: Run Passage Prep on Matthew 5:4 with complete relevant public-domain Watson and Henry commentary plus manuscript-grounded John Piper analysis. Deliver a navigable substantial PDF and HIGHLIGHT the best in-text source lines for me to study, not just a list of references.
cases.expected: Navigable PDF with full eligible historic texts and genuine exact-phrase soft-yellow highlighting in the source body, modern copyrighted sources analyzed within permission limits, and no sermon ghostwriting
assertions: Highlight annotations or visually checked yellow shading land on the original source wording itself in at least two distinct public-domain reading sections
Selections are verbatim faithful to source and appear within relevant passages, not fabricated paraphrase or only a separate highlight index
Highlight reasons favor textual, interpretive, theological, pastoral or communicative value rather than marking everything
Highlight density stays selective, roughly less than 10% of long original texts
PDF rendering and text selectability are verified for highlighted portions from beginning, middle and end
Any highlight/study trail links point to the actual source locations
Full modern copyrighted sermon transcript is not illegally reproduced simply to create highlights
No imposed AI-written final sermon
